QUSHAYRI:v3p263/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p263/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p263/r1.claim: One view says God taught human speech and that the human meant here is Muhammad; another identifies him as Adam.
QUSHAYRI:v3p263/r1.anchor: فالإنسان على هذا القول هو محمد . وقيل هو آدم عليه السلام

QUSHAYRI:v3p263/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p263/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p263/r2.claim: Ordinary human explanation is the ability to address others through likeness and form; for believers and knowers, it is knowing how to address their Lord through speech, breath, tears, longing, and sighs.
QUSHAYRI:v3p263/r2.anchor: وأما أهل الإيمان والمعرفة فبيانهم هو علمهم كيفية مخاطبة مولاهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p223#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p223#2/r9.speaker: ابن زيد والجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p223#2/r9.claim: بيان is speech, understanding, and making meaning clear verbally; this distinguishes humans from other animals.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p223#2/r9.anchor: و: البيان النطق والفهم والإبانة عن ذلك بقول قاله ابن زيد والجمهور،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p223#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p223#2/r10.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p223#2/r10.claim: Qatada specifies البيان as knowledge of lawful and unlawful matters and religious laws; the author treats this as one part of the general meaning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p223#2/r10.anchor: وقال قتادة: هو بيان الحلال والحرام والشرائع

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r6.claim: He interprets البيان as knowing lawful and unlawful matters.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r6.anchor: أن البيان الحلال والحرام , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r7.speaker: الضحاك والربيع بن أنس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r7.claim: They understand it as the ability to distinguish good and evil.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r7.anchor: الخير والشر , قاله الضحاك , والربيع بن أنس

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r8.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r8.claim: He glosses it as articulate speech.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r9.claim: Another transmitted view takes البيان as writing.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r11.claim: It may mean reason, since spoken explanation expresses what reason apprehends; more broadly, it joins expressing oneself and understanding what is explained.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r11.anchor: العقل لأن بيان اللسان مترجم عنه . ويحتمل سابعا : أن يكون البيان ما اشتمل على أمرين

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r12.speaker: بعض أصحاب الخواطر
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r12.claim: They say God created the human without knowing Him, then taught the way to Him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r12.anchor: الخواطر : خلق الإنسان جاهلا به ، فعلمه السبيل إليه

TABATABAI:55:1-30/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:1-30/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:1-30/r1.claim: Teaching humans البيان is not the revelation or inspiration of ready-made languages; social life naturally drives people to communicate through signs, sounds, speech, and language.
TABATABAI:55:1-30/r1.anchor: أن الله سبحانه وضع اللغات ثم علمها الإنسان بالوحي إلى نبي من الأنبياء أو بالإلهام

TABATABAI:55:1-30/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:1-30/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:1-30/r2.claim: God creates human nature for social life and for conventional links between words and meanings; writing then marks words and completes speech, which represents meaning.
TABATABAI:55:1-30/r2.anchor: خلق الإنسان وفطره فطرة تؤديه إلى الاجتماع المدني ثم إلى وضع اللغة بجعل اللفظ علامة للمعنى بحيث إذا ألقى اللفظ إلى سامعه

TABATABAI:55:1-30#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:1-30#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:1-30#2/r1.claim: Language is among God's greatest blessings, preserving humanity's human standing and guiding it toward good.
TABATABAI:55:1-30#2/r1.anchor: البيان من أعظم النعم والآلاء الربانية التي تحفظ لنوع الإنسان موقفه الإنساني وتهديه إلى كل خير

TABATABAI:55:1-30#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:1-30#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:1-30#2/r2.claim: Reported readings take the human as Adam and البيان as the names taught to him, or take the human as Muhammad and البيان as the Qur'an or teaching it to believers; another takes البيان as knowing good and evil. The author considers these remote.
TABATABAI:55:1-30#2/r2.anchor: فقيل الإنسان هو آدم عليه السلام والبيان الأسماء التي علمه الله إياها، وقيل الإنسان محمد صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABRISI:55:1-13/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:1-13/r15.speaker: الصادق
TABRISI:55:1-13/r15.claim: Al-Ṣādiq interprets the taught bayān as the Greatest Name through which everything was taught.
TABRISI:55:1-13/r15.anchor: قال الصادق ع: البيان الاسم الأعظم الذي به علم كل شيء

TABRISI:55:1-13/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:1-13/r16.speaker: الحسن، أبو العالية، ابن زيد، السدي
TABRISI:55:1-13/r16.claim: The human may mean all people, taught speech, writing, script, comprehension, and communication; the author calls this the broadest and most apparent view.
TABRISI:55:1-13/r16.anchor: النطق والكتابة والخط والفهم والإفهام حتى يعرف ما يقول وما يقال له عن الحسن وأبي العالية وابن زيد والسدي

TABRISI:55:1-13/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:1-13/r17.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:55:1-13/r17.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says bayān is speech that expresses intent and distinguishes humans from other animals.
TABRISI:55:1-13/r17.anchor: البيان هو الكلام الذي يبين به عن مراده وبه يتميز من سائر الحيوانات عن الجبائي

ELMALILI:55:1-13/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r15.claim: Bayan is the gift of articulate language: expressing oneself, feelings, perceptions, and will clearly to others, and understanding them; Quranic knowledge and teaching also depend on it.
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r15.anchor: kendini ve vicdan ve zamîrindeki duygu ve idrâkât ve irâdâtını

ELMALILI:55:1-13/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r16.claim: Adam learned what angels did not through the names; prophets' revelation and communication, communities' benefit from scripture, and people's access to Quran and its interpretation depend on the gift of bayan.
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r16.anchor: Hazret-i Âdem yaradıldıktan sonra ta‘lîm-i esmâ sayesinde melâikenin bilemediklerini bildi

ELMALILI:55:1-13/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r17.speaker: Ebussuud
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r17.claim: Abu Suud says teaching bayan includes understanding another person's expression, not merely being able to express oneself, since Quran teaching depends on it; the successive clauses are synonymous and omit conjunction as enumeration.
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r17.anchor: Beyânı ta‘lîmden murad, insanı mücerred kendi beyânına temkinden ibaret değil

ELMALILI:55:1-13/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r18.claim: Fronting the subject in the construction conveys restriction.
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r18.anchor: Müsned-i ileyhin takdîmi de kasr ifade eyler

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p106/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p106/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p106/r1.claim: God taught the Qur’an out of mercy; granting speech means humans can understand and teach one another, so they should use this exalted ability for instruction rather than punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p106/r1.anchor: It is the merciful nature of the Almighty because of which He has taught them the Qur’ ān

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p109/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p109/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p109/r3.claim: The sūrah opens by presenting the Qur’an as divine mercy and teaching; human creation and speech make people fit to learn through revelation rather than punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p109/r3.anchor: The sūrah begins with the declaration that the Qur’ ān is a manifestation of the graciousness of the Almighty.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p111/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p111/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p111/r2.claim: Human creation and speech imply that God intends to teach people through a guidance-giving scripture rather than torment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p111/r2.anchor: the creation of man and his abilities also require that instead of torment, a scripture of guidance be sent down.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r1.claim: Speech entails intellect: people can move between particulars and principles, reason, infer, and form opinions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r1.anchor: man has intellect, he can derive principles from parts and vice versa and simulate parts from principles.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r2.speaker: Aristotle
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r2.claim: Aristotle regards this intellectual ability as what distinguishes humans from animals; without it a person is merely a two-legged animal.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r2.anchor: Aristotle regards this ability of man as one which distinguishes him from animals.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r3.claim: Those who insist on seeing a reality before believing, despite being able to reason, are no better than animals.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r3.anchor: those who, instead of understanding a reality on the basis of reasoning, insist that they will only believe in it after seeing it are no less than animals

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r4.claim: بيان is articulate speech distinguishing humans and enabling verbal learning; a mute person cannot receive what speech conveys.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r4.anchor: ثم ذكر تعالى الوصف الذي يتميز به الإنسان من المنطق المفصح عن الضمير،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r8.speaker: ابن زيد والجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r8.claim: They define بيان as speech and understanding, distinguishing humans from other animals.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r8.anchor: وقال ابن زيد والجمهور: البيان: المنطق، والفهم: الإبانة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r9.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r9.claim: He reads بيان as clarifying lawful matters and religious laws, part of its broad meaning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r9.anchor: وقال قتادة: هو بيان الحلال والشرائع، وهذا جزء من البيان العام.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p55/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p55/r1.speaker: محمد بن كعب والضحاك وابن جريج ويمان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p55/r1.claim: They interpret بيان as what one says and hears said, good and evil, guidance, and writing, respectively.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p55/r1.anchor: ما يقول وما يقال له. وقال الضحاك: الخير والشر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p55/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p55/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p55/r2.claim: If الإنسان means Adam, بيان may mean names of things, languages especially Arabic, speech after creation, knowledge of both worlds, or the Greatest Name, attributed to Jaʿfar al-Sadiq.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p55/r2.anchor: ومن قال: الإنسان آدم، فالبيان أسماء كل شيء، أو التكلم بلغات كثيرة

BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r13.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r13.claim: God granted complete readiness to receptive people in pre-eternity; Quran names speech in its unified origin, whereas Furqan names its differentiated end, so Quran teaching does not depend on human creation, but expressive speech does.
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r13.anchor: الكلام الإلهي قرآن باعتبار الجمع والبداية وفرقان باعتبار الفرق والنهاية

BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r14.claim: The order follows this distinction: Quran teaching precedes human creation, while creating the human precedes teaching expression.
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r14.anchor: ولذا قدم تعليم القرآن على خلق الإنسان وخلقه على تعليم البيان

QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r12.claim: Here humanity means the human species: God taught people expression, distinguishing them from animals, and taught each people its language; bayān is what makes meanings clear, with its fuller explanation belonging to works on foundational principles.
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r12.anchor: ها هنا مجنس الناس ؛ علمهم البيان حتى صاروا مميزين - فانفصلوا بالبيان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda identify the human as Adam; he was taught the names of everything.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r5.anchor: {خلق الإنسان} يعني آدم عليه السلام، قاله ابن عباس وقتادة. {علمه البيان} أسماء كل شيء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r6.claim: Another interpretation says Adam learned all languages and spoke seven hundred thousand, the best of them Arabic.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r6.anchor: وقيل:علمه اللغات كلها، وكان آدم يتكلم بسبعمائة [ألف] (3) لغة أفضلها العربية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r7.speaker: أبو العالية وابن زيد والحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r7.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya, Ibn Zayd, and al-Ḥasan take human generically as all people, taught speech, writing, understanding, and communication.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r7.anchor: وقال الآخرون: "الإنسان" اسم جنس، وأراد به جميع الناس "علمه البيان" النطق والكتابة والفهم والإفهام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r8.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r8.claim: Al-Suddī says God taught each people the language they speak.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r8.anchor: وقال السدي: علم كل قوم لسانهم الذي يتكلمون به

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r9.speaker: ابن كيسان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r9.claim: Ibn Kaysān identifies the human as Muḥammad and the البيان as his disclosure of past and future events, earlier peoples, later peoples, and Judgment Day.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r9.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان: "خلق الإنسان" يعني: محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم "علمه البيان" يعني بيان ما كان وما يكون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#2/r2.claim: Al-Hasan interprets البيان as speech or pronunciation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#2/r2.anchor: قال الحسن: يعني: النطق (1) . وقال الضحاك،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#2/r3.speaker: الضحاك وقتادة وغيرهما
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#2/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak, Qatadah, and others interpret البيان as knowledge of good and evil.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#2/r3.anchor: وقال الضحاك، وقتادة، وغيرهما: يعني الخير والشر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#2/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir prefers al-Hasan's pronunciation reading: the context is teaching Quran recitation, made possible by easing speech and articulation of the letters.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#2/r4.anchor: وقول الحسن ها هنا أحسن وأقوى؛ لأن السياق في تعليمه تعالى القرآن، وهو أداء تلاوته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r1.claim: Zamakhsharī places the Quran first among divine favors because religion is the foremost favor; its revelation and teaching are the highest-ranked revelation and the summit, proof, and standard of heavenly books.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r1.anchor: وهي نعمة الدين ، فقدم من نعمة الدين ما هو في أعلى مراتبها وأقصى مراقيها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r3.claim: Human eloquent, expressive speech distinguishes people from other animals by conveying what is inward.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r3.anchor: ثم ذكر ما تميز به من سائر الحيوان من البيان ، وهو المنطق الفصيح المعرب عما في الضمير

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r4.claim: Al-Raḥmān is the subject; the following verbs with their pronouns form successive predicates without conjunctions, matching a listing of favors and making each clause an independent rebuke to deniers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r4.anchor: أخبار مترادفة ، وإخلاؤها من العاطف لمجيئها على نمط التعديد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r5.claim: He illustrates the rebuke by listing how Zayd was helped after poverty, lowliness, and scarcity, then asking what kindness he could deny.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r5.anchor: زيد أغناك بعد فقر ، أعزك بعد ذل ، كثرك بعد قلة ، فعل بك ما لم يفعل أحد بأحد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r10.claim: The first clauses omit conjunctions so each independently rebukes deniers by enumerating benefactions; conjunctions resume for clauses that suit and approach each other.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r10.anchor: ثم رد الكلام إلى منهاجه بعد التبكيت في وصل ما يجب وصله للتناسب والتقارب بالعاطف

MUQATIL:55:1-4/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:55:1-4/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:55:1-4/r2.claim: The al-Rahman whom they denied taught the Qur'an, created Adam, and taught him speech—the explanation of all things.
MUQATIL:55:1-4/r2.anchor: فقال: { الرحمن } الذي أنكروه هو الذي { علم القرآن خلق الإنسان } [آية: 3] يعني آدم

QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r8.claim: One view says God taught the human the names of everything.

QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r9.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r9.claim: Another view takes البيان to mean all languages.

QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r11.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r11.claim: Another view says البيان is what was and what will be, since the Prophet told about earlier and later people and Judgment Day.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r11.anchor: وقيل: ما كان وما يكون لأنه بين عن الأولين والآخرين ويوم الدين

QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r12.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r12.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says البيان is good and evil.

QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r13.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r13.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas and Qatāda say البيان is what benefits a person and what harms him.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r13.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس: هو ما ينفعه وما يضره وقاله قتادة

QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r15.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r15.claim: Al-Suddī says each people were taught the language they speak.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r15.anchor: وقال السدي: علم كل قوم لسانهم الذي يتكلمون به

QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r16.speaker: يمان
QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r16.claim: Yamān identifies البيان as writing with the pen, linked to 96:4–5.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r16.anchor:
وقال يمان: الكتابة والخط بالقلم. نظيره:
علم بالقلم. علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم

RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r6.claim: The order in al-‘Alaq differs only because it does not explicitly mention teaching the Qur’an; its creation-before-teaching sequence corresponds to ‘created humanity, taught him expression’ here.
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r6.anchor: في تلك السورة لم يصرح بتعليم القرآن فهو كالتعليم الذي ذكره في هذه السورة بقوله : { علمه البيان } بعد قوله : { خلق الإنسان }

RAZI-FULL:v29p76/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p76/r3.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v29p76/r3.claim: Some exegetes say البيان means speech: God taught humans what to utter and how to make their thoughts understood, distinguishing them from animals.
RAZI-FULL:v29p76/r3.anchor: من المفسرين من قال : البيان المنطق فعلمه ما ينطق به ويفهم غيره ما عنده

RAZI-FULL:v29p76/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p76/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p76/r4.claim: On the speech reading, creating the human refers to forming the distinctive body, while teaching expression distinguishes humans through knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v29p76/r4.anchor: إشارة إلى تقدير خلق جسمه الخاص

RAZI-FULL:v29p76/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p76/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p76/r5.claim: Al-Razi’s earlier view takes البيان as the Qur’an, elaborating the concise mention of Qur’an teaching; the Qur’an calls itself ‘a clarification for people’ because it separates truth from falsehood.
RAZI-FULL:v29p76/r5.anchor: البيان هو القرآن وأعاده ليفصل ماذكره إجمالا بقوله تعالى : { علم القرءان }

RAZI-FULL:v29p76/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p76/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p76/r6.claim: If Qur’an teaching is to humanity, the second object is omitted to exalt the favor and to present it before the recipient’s creation and the explanation of its manner.
RAZI-FULL:v29p76/r6.anchor: حذفه لعظم نعمة التعليم وقدم ذكره على من علمه وعلى بيان خلقه

RAZI-FULL:v29p76/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p76/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p76/r7.claim: If the Qur’an was taught to angels, the human recipient is stated explicitly because that teaching is an evident favor to people, whereas angelic teaching does not visibly benefit them.
RAZI-FULL:v29p76/r7.anchor: وتعليمه للملائكة لا يظهر للإنسان أنه فائدة

RAZI-FULL:v29p76/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p76/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p76/r8.claim: The contrast resembles al-‘Alaq: first God teaches with the pen without naming the recipient, then explicitly teaches humanity what it did not know.
RAZI-FULL:v29p76/r8.anchor: قال مرة : { علم بالقلم } من غير بيان المعلم ، ثم قال مرة أخرى : { علم الإنسان لم يعلم }

RAZI-FULL:v29p76/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p76/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p76/r9.claim: Al-Razi says this verse may support the view that languages were instituted through God’s teaching.
RAZI-FULL:v29p76/r9.anchor: ويحتمل أن يتمسك بهذه الآية على أن اللغات توقيفية حصل العلم بها بتعليم الله

ZAJJAJ:v5p95/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p95/r3.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v5p95/r3.claim: One interpretation identifies the human as the Prophet, whom God taught the Qurʾān containing clarification of everything.
ZAJJAJ:v5p95/r3.anchor: قيل إنه يعني بالإنسان ههنا النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - علمه البيان. علمه القرآن الذي فيه بيان كل شيء.

ZAJJAJ:v5p95/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p95/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p95/r5.claim: The word may mean humanity as a species; on that reading, teaching them expression made humans distinct from other animals.
ZAJJAJ:v5p95/r5.anchor: ويجوز في اللغة أن يكون الإنسان اسما لجنس الناس جميعا، ويكون على هذا المعنى علمه البيان جعله مميزا حتى انفصل الإنسان من جميع الحيوان.

THALABI:v9p177#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p177#2/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p177#2/r4.claim: One explanation of البيان is that Adam learned the names of everything; another says he learned all languages, and Adam spoke seven hundred thousand, with Arabic the best.
THALABI:v9p177#2/r4.anchor: علمه البيان أسماء كل شيء، وقيل: علمه اللغات كلها، وكان آدم عليه السلام يتكلم بسبعمائة ألف لغة أفضلها العربية

THALABI:v9p177#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p177#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v9p177#2/r6.claim: Qatada says البيان teaches lawful and unlawful matters, good and evil, and what to do or avoid, giving people grounds for accountability.
THALABI:v9p177#2/r6.anchor: فروي عن قتادة أنه قال: علمه بيان الحلال والحرام، وبين له الخير والشر، وما يأتي وما يذر

THALABI:v9p177#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p177#2/r7.speaker: أبو العالية ومرة الهمذاني وابن زيد
THALABI:v9p177#2/r7.claim: Abu al-Aliya, Murra al-Hamadhani, and Ibn Zayd interpret البيان as speech.
THALABI:v9p177#2/r7.anchor: وقال أبو العالية ومرة الهمذاني وابن زيد: يعني الكلام.

THALABI:v9p177#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p177#2/r8.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v9p177#2/r8.claim: Al-Hasan interprets البيان as speech articulation and discernment.

THALABI:v9p177#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p177#2/r9.speaker: محمد بن كعب
THALABI:v9p177#2/r9.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says البيان is what a person says and what is said to that person.
THALABI:v9p177#2/r9.anchor: محمد ابن كعب: ما يقول وما يقال له.

THALABI:v9p177#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p177#2/r10.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v9p177#2/r10.claim: Al-Suddi says God taught each people the language they speak.
THALABI:v9p177#2/r10.anchor: السدي: علم كل قوم لسانهم الذي يتكلمون به.

THALABI:v9p177#2/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p177#2/r11.speaker: يمان
THALABI:v9p177#2/r11.claim: Yaman interprets البيان as writing with the pen, as in “He taught by the pen.”
THALABI:v9p177#2/r11.anchor: يمان: الكتابة والخط بالقلم. نظيره علم بالقلم.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r6.claim: “Created the human” is coordinated as another assertion confirming the preceding statement, without a conjunction.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r6.anchor: ثم نسق على هذا خبرا آخر مؤكدا له من غير حرف عطف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r7.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r7.claim: The human created is Muhammad, and the taught expression is eloquent speech, meaning the Qur’an.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r7.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: يريد محمدا -صلى الله عليه وسلم-

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r8.speaker: ابن كيسان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r8.claim: He also identifies the human as Muhammad, but says the taught expression is knowledge of past and future events, including Judgment Day.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r8.anchor: إلا أنه قال في البيان أنه بيان ما كان وما يكون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r9.speaker: الكلبي وقتادة ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r9.claim: They identify the human as Adam, to whom God taught the names of everything.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r9.anchor: وقال الكلبي وقتادة: الإنسان آدم -عليه السلام- علمه أسماء كل شيء، وهذا قول مقاتل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r10.speaker: أبو العالية ومرة وابن زيد والحسن والقرظي والسدي ويمان بن رباب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r10.claim: They take “the human” as humankind collectively and “expression” as speech, discernment, writing, understanding, communication, and the language given to each people, distinguishing humans from animals.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r10.anchor: وقال آخرون: الإنسان اسم لجنس الناس جميعا، ومعنى {علمه البيان} النطق والتمييز، والكتابة والخط

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:1-5/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:1-5/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:1-5/r4.claim: The البيان taught is the Qur’an, which explains everything.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:1-5/r4.anchor: علمه البيان } القرآن الذي فيه بيان كل شيء.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:1-5/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:1-5/r5.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:1-5/r5.claim: An alternative identifies the human as Adam’s child and says God taught him speech, distinguishing humans from other animals.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:1-5/r5.anchor: وقيل: { خلق الإنسان } يعني ابن آدم، فعلمه النطق، وفضله به على سائر الحيوان.

STUDYQURAN:55:4/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:4/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:4/r1.claim: Human beings are distinguished from other creatures by speech, which lets them articulate and comprehend, as well as by knowing revelation.
STUDYQURAN:55:4/r1.anchor: they distinguished from all other creatures by the faculty of speech through which they both articulate and comprehend

STUDYQURAN:55:4/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:4/r2.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:55:4/r2.claim: Verses 2–4 can allude to God's honoring humanity by enabling people to learn and recite the Quran, His Word, as in 44:58 and 54:17, 22, 32, and 40.
STUDYQURAN:55:4/r2.anchor: allusion to God’s honoring human beings by making the Quran, His very Word, something they are capable of learning and reciting (Q)

STUDYQURAN:55:4/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:4/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:4/r3.claim: Bayān means speech and also something clear or evident.
STUDYQURAN:55:4/r3.anchor: Speech translates bayān, which also means something that is clear or evident.

STUDYQURAN:55:4/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:4/r4.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:55:4/r4.claim: Some understand bayān as alluding to God's teaching Adam all the names, as in 2:31.
STUDYQURAN:55:4/r4.anchor: seen by some as an allusion to God’s having taught Adam the names, all of them (2:31; see 2:31c)

STUDYQURAN:55:4/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:4/r5.speaker: Q, Sh
STUDYQURAN:55:4/r5.claim: Another proposed sense is God's teaching people to distinguish good from evil, permitted from forbidden, and truth from falsehood through revelation.
STUDYQURAN:55:4/r5.anchor: distinguish between good and evil, between what is permitted and what is forbidden (Q, Sh) or between truth and falsehood

STUDYQURAN:55:4/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:4/r6.speaker: Q, R
STUDYQURAN:55:4/r6.claim: Bayān is also regarded as a name of the Quran, as in 3:138, which calls it an exposition for humankind.
STUDYQURAN:55:4/r6.anchor: Bayān is also considered one of the names of the Quran (Q, R), as in 3:138

TAB-FULL:v22p170/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p170/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v22p170/r1.claim: Qatada says God taught people to distinguish worldly and afterlife matters, including the lawful and unlawful, as evidence against them.

TAB-FULL:v22p170/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p170/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v22p170/r2.claim: In another wording, Qatada says البيان shows people good and evil and what to do or leave.
TAB-FULL:v22p170/r2.anchor: أبو العوام، عن قتادة، في قوله: {علمه البيان}

TAB-FULL:v22p170/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p170/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v22p170/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses البيان as speech.
TAB-FULL:v22p170/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {علمه البيان}

TAB-FULL:v22p170/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p170/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p170/r4.claim: Tabari holds that God taught people all the expression and knowledge they need for religion and worldly life, including lawful and unlawful matters, livelihoods, and speech; the unrestricted wording is general.
TAB-FULL:v22p170/r4.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك أن يقال: معنى ذلك أن الله علم الإنسان ما به الحاجة إليه من أمر دينه ودنياه

BURSEVI:v9p236/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p236/r2.speaker: أبو السعود
BURSEVI:v9p236/r2.claim: Abu al-Suʿud argues the Quran is uncreated: it is mentioned in 54 places without being called created, while humanity is mentioned 18 times as created; the two are paired here.
BURSEVI:v9p236/r2.anchor: قاله المولى أبو السعود رحمه الله

BURSEVI:v9p236/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p236/r4.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v9p236/r4.claim: Al-Raghib defines bayan as disclosure; it is broader than speech, which is peculiar to humans, and speech is called bayan because it reveals the intended meaning.
BURSEVI:v9p236/r4.anchor: البيان الكشف عن الشيء وهو أعم من النطق لأن النطق مختص بالإنسان

BURSEVI:v9p236/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p236/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p236/r5.claim: Teaching bayan includes enabling a person both to express their own thoughts and to understand another person's expression, which underlies Quranic instruction.
BURSEVI:v9p236/r5.anchor: بل منه ومن فهم بيان غيره أيضا إذ هو الذي يدور عليه تعليم القرآن

BURSEVI:v9p236/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p236/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p236/r6.claim: The human in the verse means humankind as a genus, encompassing all its kinds and individuals.
BURSEVI:v9p236/r6.anchor: والمراد به جنس الإنسان الشامل لجميع أصنافه وأفراده

BURSEVI:v9p236/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p236/r7.speaker: بحر العلوم
BURSEVI:v9p236/r7.claim: Bahr al-ʿUlum takes the created human to be Adam, whom God taught all names and languages.
BURSEVI:v9p236/r7.anchor: وفي بحر العلوم خلق الإنسان أي آدم وعلمه الأسماء واللغات كلها

BURSEVI:v9p236/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p236/r8.speaker: بحر العلوم
BURSEVI:v9p236/r8.claim: Bahr al-ʿUlum says Adam spoke 700,000 languages, with Arabic the best of them.
BURSEVI:v9p236/r8.anchor: وكان آدم يتكلم بسبعمائة ألف لغة أفضلها العربية انتهى

QASHANI:55:3-6/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:55:3-6/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:55:3-6/r2.claim: Bayān is articulate speech distinguishing humans from other creatures, by which they express the Quranic intellect within.
QASHANI:55:3-6/r2.anchor: أي: النطق المميز إياه عن جميع ما سواه من المخلوقات

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:3/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:3/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:3/r1.claim: God is identified as humanity's creator, and the most important gift is the ability to express feelings and thoughts through speech and communication.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:3/r1.anchor: İnsanı da yaratanın Allah olduğu belirtilip ona verilen özelliklerin en önemlisinin, duygu ve düşüncelerini açıklayabilme, konuşma ve anlatma yetisi olduğuna işaret edilmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:3/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:3/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:3/r2.claim: Since understanding is necessary for expression, the gift emphasized is both cognition and expression: the practical face of human intellect and reasoning.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:3/r2.anchor: Anlamak, anlatabilmenin ön şartı olduğuna göre burada altı çizilen nimetin idrak ve ifade yetisi olduğu söylenebilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:3/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:3/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:3/r3.claim: Understanding and expression let people recognize and articulate worship of God and their rights and duties toward others; they allow intellect to bear fruit and form the basis of culture and civilization.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:3/r3.anchor: İnsanın, her şeyden önce Allah’a olan kulluğunu idrak ve ifade etmesi, başka insanlarla ilişkilerinde hak ve vecîbelerini kavrayıp bunların gereğini yerine getirmesi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:3/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:3/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:3/r4.claim: Laughter, tears, expressions of love or hate, meaningful speech, turning thought into action, and shaping art are all results and forms of expression.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:3/r4.anchor: Gülme, ağlama, sevgi veya nefretle bakma, anlamlı söz söyleme, düşündüklerini eyleme dönüştürme, bir sanat eserine şekil verme ... hep anlama ve anlatma faaliyetinin sonuçlarıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:3/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:3/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:3/r5.claim: Rhetorical and narrative theories, expressionism, and debates about them concretely show the importance of this human capacity, which can be exercised in any field and is especially vivid in visual arts.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:3/r5.anchor: belâgat, hitabet, beyân, narratoloji gibi teorik incelemeler; en güçlü örneklerine görsel sanatlarda rastlanmakla beraber esasen herhangi bir alanda anlatım imkânlarını zorlayan sanat akımı ekspresyonizm

BAQILLANI:v1p274/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p274/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p274/r1.claim: Bayān has four forms—speech, condition, gesture, and sign—and people differ in their degree of clarity; the verse about God teaching bayān exemplifies this capacity.
BAQILLANI:v1p274/r1.anchor: وأما حسن البيان فالبيان على أربعة أقسام كلام وحال وإشارة وعلامة

BAQILLANI:v1p274/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p274/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p274/r2.claim: The opposite of clear expression is inability to communicate; the tale of Bāqil, who loses a gazelle while trying to indicate eleven with his fingers and tongue, illustrates it.
BAQILLANI:v1p274/r2.anchor: ونقيضه العي ومنه قيل أعيا من باقل سئل عن ظبية في يده

BAQILLANI:v1p281/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p281/r1.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
BAQILLANI:v1p281/r1.claim: Abu Bakr judged Musaylima’s utterance to be speech that did not come from God, illustrating how speech from divine sovereignty is distinguished from other speech.
BAQILLANI:v1p281/r1.anchor: إن هذا كلام لم يخرج من إل

BAQILLANI:v1p281/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p281/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p281/r2.claim: The Qur’an’s bayan is the noblest, most rightly guiding, complete, elevated, eloquent, and radiant form of expression.
BAQILLANI:v1p281/r2.anchor: ثم رجع الكلام بنا إلى ما ابتدأنا به من عظيم شأن البيان ولو لم يكن فيه إلا ما من به الله على خلقه بقوله

BURHAN:v1p312/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p312/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p312/r1.claim: Knowledge of rhetoric's forms is central to exegesis and eloquence; the author says God's teaching of the Qur'an and human speech alone would suffice to show the honor of eloquence.
BURHAN:v1p312/r1.anchor: واعلم أن معرفة هذه الصناعة بأوضاعها هى عمدة التفسير المطلع على عجائب كلام الله وهى قاعدة الفصاحة وواسطة عقد البلاغة

BURHAN:v1p312/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p312/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p312/r2.claim: The author invokes “This is a clear statement for people” and “a clarification of all things” as further scriptural praise of البيان.
BURHAN:v1p312/r2.anchor: وقال تعالى ﴿ هذا بيان للناس ﴾ وقال تعالى ﴿ تبيانا لكل شيء ﴾

BURHAN:v1p312/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p312/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p312/r3.claim: The omitted conjunction in “He taught him clear speech” places teaching speech alongside creating humanity, almost as a substitute, since the human is a living speaker.
BURHAN:v1p312/r3.anchor: ولحذف الواو فى قوله تعالى ﴿ علمه البيان ﴾ نكتة علمية فإنه جعل تعليم البيان فى وزان خلقه وكالبدل من قوله ﴿ خلق الإنسان ﴾

BURHAN:v1p312/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p312/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p312/r4.claim: Rhetorical skill strengthens understanding and persuasion, enabling the hearer to accept and submit to what is argued.
BURHAN:v1p312/r4.anchor: وهى قاعدة الفصاحة وواسطة عقد البلاغة ولو لم يحبب الفصاحة إلا قول الله تعالى

SULAMI:v2p293#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p293#2/r2.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p293#2/r2.claim: Sahl describes bayan as speech, the mind of creatures and essence of spirit, and associates intellect with understanding, the heart with discernment, and the self with nature.
SULAMI:v2p293#2/r2.anchor: قال سهل في قوله : ﴿ علمه البيان ﴾ أي الكلام الذي هو ذهن الخلق ونفس الروح فهم العقل

SULAMI:v2p293#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p293#2/r3.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p293#2/r3.claim: The spirit was disclosed in pre-eternity; bayan is the disclosure of that prior teaching, which had already preceded.
SULAMI:v2p293#2/r3.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : ﴿ خلق الإنسان علمه البيان ﴾ . قال : كاشف روحه قديما والبيان لا يكون إلا بكشف ما تقدم

SULAMI:v2p293#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p293#2/r4.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p293#2/r4.claim: God created the human being ignorant of Him, then taught him the way to Him.
SULAMI:v2p293#2/r4.anchor: وقال الجنيد : خلق الإنسان جاهل به فعلمه السبيل إليه

SULAMI:v2p293#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p293#2/r5.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p293#2/r5.claim: A human consists of remembrance and reflection: if directed to self-interest, both cut one off from God; if for and through God, they connect one to Him, purify the senses, and let the clear heart behold His dominion. More remembrance and reflection bring more nearness and knowledge.
SULAMI:v2p293#2/r5.anchor: وقال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : الإنسان شيئان ذكر وفكر فإن كان ذكره وفكره إلى حظ نفسه انقطع عن الله

TUSTARI:55:4/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:55:4/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:55:4/r1.claim: God taught Adam speech arising from spirit, rational understanding, heart discernment, human thought, and natural disposition, then clarified it.
TUSTARI:55:4/r1.anchor: يعني علمه الكلام الذي هو من نفس الروح وفهم العقل وفطنة القلب وذهن الخلق وعلم نفس الطبع

RUMMANI:v1p106/r5.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p106/r5.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p106/r5.claim: Since God praises bayān, one should not apply the unqualified term to ugly speech; it is acceptable when qualified as merely making an intended meaning understood.
RUMMANI:v1p106/r5.anchor: وليس بحسن أن يطلق اسم بيان على ما قبح من الكلام

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p436#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p436#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p436#2/r1.claim: He explains bayān as speech or language.

ASAD-NOTES:55:1#n1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:1#n1/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:1#n1/r1.claim: Al-bayan means making something intellectually circumscribed and clear (Raghib), covering thought that distinguishes concepts and clear expression in speech or writing (Taj al-'Arus).
ASAD-NOTES:55:1#n1/r1.anchor: al-bayan - denoting "the means whereby a thing is [intellectually] circumscribed and made clear" (Raghib) - applies to both thought and speech

ASAD-NOTES:55:1#n1/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:1#n1/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:1#n1/r2.claim: In context al-bayan is articulate thought and speech, recalling man's God-given conceptual faculty, the knowledge of all names.
ASAD-NOTES:55:1#n1/r2.anchor: hence, in the above context, "articulate thought and speech", recalling the "knowledge of all the names"

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p590/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p590/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p590/r2.claim: The author says the human is singled out because he received the revealed book and explains it to both groups; البيان is the ability to express what is within oneself.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p590/r2.anchor: الإنسان هو الذي أُنزل عليه الكتاب أو القرآن وبيّنه للثقلين. وعلّمه البيان بمعنى ليبيّن عن نفسه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1044/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1044/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1044/r1.claim: The Qur'an is named before human creation because it is the book of worship, and worship is the purpose for which humans and jinn were created; purpose precedes the work it governs.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1044/r1.anchor: فلما كان خلق الإنسان والجن لغرض العبادة والقرآن هو كتاب العبادة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1044/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1044/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1044/r3.claim: The Qur'an is prior in purpose, existence, and merit; Qur'anic order need not be chronological and may instead follow context, priority, or excellence, sometimes placing a later event first.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1044/r3.anchor: إذا كان على الفضل هو أسبق وإذا كان على الزمن هو أسبق وإذا كان على العلة والغرض هو أسبق

ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r1.claim: Here البيان is articulate, eloquent speech that expresses what is within; it is the ordinary means by which people learn the Qur’an.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r1.anchor: لأن البيان هو الذي بهيتمكن عادة من تعلم القرآن المراد به المنطق الفصيح المعرب عما في الضمير

ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r2.speaker: الإرشاد
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r2.claim: Al-Irshad reads creation of the human as identifying the learner and teaching البيان as explaining how the teaching occurs.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r2.anchor: وفي الإرشاد أن قوله تعالى : ( خلق الإنسان ) تعيين للمتعلم

ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r3.claim: Teaching البيان means enabling people to express themselves and understand others, since that capacity underlies instruction in the Qur’an.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r3.anchor: والمراد بتعليم البيان تمكين الإنسان من بيان نفسه ومن فهم بيان غيرهإذ

ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r4.claim: On the view that an object is omitted, the ones taught first may be the angels, who learned the Qur’an before the human was created.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r4.anchor: وقيل : بناءا على تنقدير المفعول المحذوف الملائكة المقربين إن تقديم تعليم القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r5.claim: The sequence elegantly pairs heavenly matters with earthly ones; this arrangement also works if the omitted object is Gabriel.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r5.anchor: وفي النظم الجليل عليه حسن زائد حيث أنه تعالى ذكر أموراعلوية وأموراسفلية

ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r6.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak explains البيان as good and evil.

ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r7.claim: Ibn Jurayj explains البيان as the path of guidance and the path of error.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r7.anchor: وقال ابن جريج : سبيل الهدى وسبيل الضلالة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r8.speaker: يمان
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r8.claim: Yaman explains البيان as writing; the author dismisses these alternative glosses.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r8.anchor: وقال يمان : الكتابة والكل كما ترى

ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r9.claim: A possible gloss is the Qur’an itself, called a clarification elsewhere and repeated here to unpack the earlier statement about teaching the Qur’an; the author calls this very remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r9.anchor: وجوز أن يراد به القرآنوقد سماه الله تعالى بيانا في قوله سبحانه : ( هذا بيان )

ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r10.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r10.claim: Qatadah takes the human to be Adam and البيان to be knowledge of this world and the next.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r10.anchor: وقال قتادة : ( الإنسان ) آدم و ( البيان ) علم الدنيا والآخرة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r11.claim: Other reported explanations are that البيان comprises the names of all things or the ability to speak many languages.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r11.anchor: وقيل : ( البيان ) أسماء الأشياء كلها وقيل : التكلم بلغات كثيرة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r12.speaker: جعفر الصادق
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r12.claim: A view attributed to Ja‘far al-Sadiq identifies البيان as the Greatest Name by which everything was taught.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r12.anchor: وقيل : الاسم الأعظم الذي علم به كل شيء ونسبهذا إلى جعفر الصادق

ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r13.speaker: ابن كسيان
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r13.claim: Ibn Kaysan identifies the human as Muhammad and takes البيان as explaining revelation, clarifying the Qur’an’s general or ambiguous passages, or the Qur’an itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r13.anchor: وقالابن كسيان : ( الإنسان ) محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r14.claim: The author prefers the immediately apparent reading: the human generally is taught expressive speech, rather than the reported specialized meanings.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r14.anchor: المتبادر من الآيات الكريمة لا يخفى عليك ولا أظنك في مرية من تبادر ما ذكرناه فيها أولا

ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r15.claim: The clauses about creating the human and teaching البيان each predicate something of the implicit subject الرحمن, as does teaching the Qur’an.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p99#2/r15.anchor: ثم إن كلا من الجملتين الأخيرتين خبر عن المبتدأكجملة ( علم القرآن )

BIQAI-FULL:v7p373/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p373/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p373/r2.claim: Bayān is the human rational and speaking faculty: it grasps particulars and universals, infers absent matters from present ones by signs or calculation, distinguishes good from evil, and communicates thought through speech, action, writing, and gesture.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p373/r2.anchor: وهي الإدراك للأأمور الكلية والجزئية والحكم الحاضر والغائب

BIQAI-FULL:v7p373/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p373/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p373/r3.claim: This faculty enables people to perfect themselves and teach others, making bayān the means for learning the Qur'an; its familiarity to humans should not obscure its extraordinary divine gift, displayed in Adam's knowledge before the angels.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p373/r3.anchor: فصار بذلك ذا قدرة على الكمال في نفسه والتكميل لغيره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r15.speaker: الكشاف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r15.claim: The Kashshaf says the sura leads with the greatest religious favor, Quranic revelation and teaching, then human creation and the distinctive gift of expression.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r15.anchor: قال في ( الكشاف ) : ( أراد الله أن يقدم في عدد آلائه أول شيء ما هو أسبق قدما من ضروب آلائه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r3.claim: The sura recalls God's power in perfected creation while drawing attention to the favors creation gives humanity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r3.anchor: ثم التذكير بدلائل قدرة الله تعالى فيما أتقن صنعه مدمجا في ذلك التذكير بما في ذلك كله من نعم على الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r7.claim: Humanity depends on God's mercy through created favors, especially knowledge and expression, while the sura contrasts punishment for sinners with reward and honor for the pious.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r7.anchor: ومن أهمها نعمة العلم ونعمة البيان ، وما أعد من الجزاء للمجرمين ومن الثواب والكرامة للمتقين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r4.claim: The sura counts great worldly favors for all and afterlife favors for believers, and leads with religion because it reforms worldly life and brings success in the next.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r4.anchor: وقد عدد الله في هذه السورة نعما عظيمة على الناس كلهم في الدنيا ، وعلى المؤمنين خاصة في الآخرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan says bayān is speech and discernment.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r2.claim: Qatāda says bayān is knowledge of what is lawful and unlawful.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r3.speaker: محمد بن كعب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r3.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb says bayān is what a person says and what is said to him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r3.anchor: والثالث ما يقول وما يقال له قاله محمد بن كعب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r4.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says bayān is the distinction between good and evil.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj says bayān is the paths of guidance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r5.anchor: والخامس طرق الهدى قاله ابن جريج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r6.speaker: يمان
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r6.claim: Yamān says bayān is writing and script.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r7.claim: If ‘the human’ in the preceding verse means Adam, bayān has three reported explanations: names of everything, explaining everything, or languages.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r7.anchor: أنه آدم قاله ابن عباس وقتادة فعلى هذا في البيان ثلاثة أقوال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r8.speaker: غير مسمى
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r8.claim: On the Adam interpretation, one view says bayān is the names of everything.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r8.anchor: أحدها أسماء كل شيء والثاني بيان كل شيء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r9.speaker: غير مسمى
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r9.claim: On the Adam interpretation, a second view says bayān is explaining everything.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r9.anchor: والثاني بيان كل شيء والثالث اللغات

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r10.speaker: غير مسمى
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r10.claim: On the Adam interpretation, a third view says bayān is languages.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r11.speaker: ابن كيسان
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r11.claim: A third view says the human is Muhammad, whom God taught to explain what has been and what will be.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106#3/r11.anchor: والقول الثالث أنه محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم علمه بيان ما كان وما يكون

NASAFI-FULL:v4p199#8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p199#8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p199#8/r1.claim: In enumerating favors, Allah first mentions the foremost religious blessing: revealing and teaching the Qur'an, the highest and most beneficial revelation and the standard confirming the other scriptures; human creation follows because humanity was created for religion and knowledge of revelation.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p199#8/r1.anchor: عدد الله عز وجل آلاءه فاراد ان يقدم اول شىء ما هو اسبق قدما من ضروب آلائه وصنوف نعمائه وهى نعمة الدين فقدم من عمة الدين

NASAFI-FULL:v4p199#8/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p199#8/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p199#8/r2.claim: After that, Allah mentions the human distinction from other animals: clear, eloquent speech that expresses what is inward.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p199#8/r2.anchor: ثم ذكر ما تميز به من سائر الحيوان من البيان وهو المنطق الفصيح العرب عما في الضمير

NASAFI-FULL:v4p199#8/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p199#8/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p199#8/r3.claim: Al-Raḥmān is the subject; the following verbs with their pronouns are successive predicates, left uncoordinated as an enumeration, like a series of favors attributed to Zayd.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p199#8/r3.anchor: والرحمن مبتدا وهذه الافعال مع ضمائرها اخبار مترادفة واخلاؤها من العاطف لمجيئها على نمط التعديد كما تقول زيد اغناك بعد فقر
